newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-New Australis debt assigned B2 rating.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-New Australis debt assigned B2 rating.

text.p: Ratings agency Moody's Investors Service said on Thursday it had assigned its B2 rating to Australis Media Ltd's new offering of US$150 million of senior secured discount notes due 2002.
Moody's also said it confirmed the Caa rating on Australis' previously issued US$175 million of senior subordinated notes due 2003.
The confirmation concluded a review of the pay television operator's existing debt which began on March 19, it said.

"The ratings reflect the undeveloped status of the Australian pay television market, Australis' highly leveraged position, limited financial flexibility and exposure to the pricing actions of its competitors," Moody's said.
"The ratings also anticipate the successful completion of Australis' refinancing, including an additional US$100 million in new equity, which would alleviate near term liquidity pressures," it said.

The ratings also incorporated the beneficial effects of Australis' agreement to provide programming to Foxtel, a cable television joint venture owned by News Corp Ltd and the state-owned telecommunications firm, Telstra Corp.
"The B2 rating assigned to the new notes reflects the notes first ranking lien over the collateral assets of Australis and its gauaranteed subsidiaries," Moody's said.

It said that high demand for subscription services, increased competitive pricing pressures, continuing operating losses and the need to fund the rapid deployment of infrastructure had resulted in a significant rise in leverage and a liquidity crisis at Australis.
But management had now refocused the business on providing subscription services in areas where cable broadband services would not be widely available for at least the next few years.

"Moody's expecst that the new business strategy, in tandem with the previous installation and subscription price increases, will result in lower subscriber growth, reduced churn and a reduction in the drain on cash reserves from connection subsidiaries involved in the provison of Australis' satelite and microwave pay-tv services," Moody's said.
It also said the pay television industry could be rationalised over the medium term.

Following the recapitalisation, Lenfest Communications Inc, 50 percent owned by Tele-Communications Inc, will have a 32.8 percent economic interest in Australis and Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd will have a 10 percent economic interest in Australis.
Other shareholders include the AMP Society, Guiness Peat Group Plc and United International Holdings Inc.
